100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 11, 1926, a significant political shift occurred in the United Kingdom as Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin called for a general election, aiming to solidify his Conservative government amidst growing tensions in the labor movement. Meanwhile, in the United States, the ongoing debate surrounding Prohibition intensified as calls for repeal gained traction, reflecting a nation increasingly divided over the alcohol ban. In international news, tensions continued to mount in the Middle East, particularly in Palestine, where escalating violence raised alarms about stability in the region.
